summary: WoW-style bags (the owner, 2026-10-03: "can we do the inventory similar to world of warcraft with the bags and etc?", then "WoW-style bags ... i just need you to do these"): a slot layout over the pack (PlayerBags, scripts/inventory/bags.gd). The haversack is always worn; four sockets on the bag bar take the bag items below. A slot holds one stack of one kind up to its stack size; a specialty bag holds only its own kinds. What fits nowhere rides loose and slows the player. Every number is a design value (basis D) and tunable. 1750s things, drawn and named our own way: none of them is a medicine bag or a bundle (sacred objects of living Native traditions), and the bow's worn quiver stays the loadout piece it is.

haversack.name: Haversack
haversack.text: A linen haversack slung at the hip: the base pack, always worn.

linen_satchel.name: Linen Satchel
linen_satchel.got: every new game starts with one (a start with nothing: none)

knapsack.name: Knapsack
knapsack.text: A painted canvas or goatskin knapsack, as soldiers and rangers carried.
knapsack.got: the workbench (2 buckskin, a cord, tallow), the sutler and the visiting trader, a fallen soldier's things

blanket_roll.name: Blanket Roll
blanket_roll.text: A wool blanket rolled round your things and slung.
blanket_roll.got: the workbench: a wool blanket from your kit (not worn) and a cord

portmanteau.name: Portmanteau
portmanteau.text: A leather portmanteau. Rare up the valley.

hunting_pouch.name: Hunting Pouch
hunting_pouch.got: the workbench (buckskin and a sinew), a fallen militiaman's things

game_bag.name: Game Bag
game_bag.text: A netted game bag on a rawhide band.

simples_bag.name: Simples Bag
simples_bag.text: An herb pouch (simples: the period word for medicinal plants).

holds._doc: What a specialty bag takes (pack kinds; a kind not in the game yet is harmless: the shot pouch's balls, shot, patches and powder, for when they are pack things; the powder horn stays gear). 'text' is what ItemInfo and a refusal say.

shot.text: shot and its makings: balls, shot, flints, patches, bar lead, the bullet mould, flint and steel, powder

game.text: game: meat, fish, small game, pelts, hides, antler, bone, tallow, brains, sinew

simples.text: simples: herbs, barks, roots, berries, remedies, seed, tobacco

stacks._doc: How many of a kind one slot holds: 'default' unless the kind is listed. Heavy things 1-5 (logs, poles, a buffalo robe, the canoe's parts), small things 50 (flints, feathers, seed). A garment carried (kind 'cloth:<item>') is one a slot; a bag not worn is one a slot.

loose._doc: Full bags: what fits nowhere rides loose, a stack a loose slot. Each slows the player 'slow_each' (at most 'slow_max'), multiplied into the speed the survival bridge feeds; from 'no_sprint_at' loose slots there is no sprint.

start._doc: The sockets a new game starts with (socket 1 first); a start with nothing: 'bare'. A save from before the bags loads with 'start'.

loot._doc: What a fallen fighter's pack sometimes holds (NpcFighter._loot_items: faction id -> bag kind -> the chance, rolled once each): soldiers a knapsack, the woodsmen of the Canadian militia a hunting pouch.

trade._doc: The bags the traders sell, as the survival core's items (data/survival/items.json, economy.json: the sutler sells the knapsack, the visiting trader the knapsack and the portmanteau). Bought, they come into the pack (SurvivalBridge, on the core's trade_committed).
